title: Fix [Latest Match Rate] and [Latest Coverage Rate] — both BLANK by construction
description:
Both quality measures return BLANK in every filter context. This is a computation defect, not a data gap, and it is already diagnosed with live measurements in docs/dax_measure_library.md:235 (written under task-061, 2026-08-11) — read that note first rather than re-deriving it.

Root cause: `VAR LatestRun = MAXX(gold_quality_history, gold_quality_history[refresh_timestamp])` takes the max over the WHOLE table, but two notebooks append to gold_quality_history in the same pipeline run, each stamping its own pipeline_run_ts. `silver_to_gold` writes coverage_rate / match_rate; `data_quality_checks` then writes only dq_* rows roughly ten minutes later. The later timestamp therefore always wins and never carries either metric, so the `refresh_timestamp = LatestRun` and `metric_name = "..."` filters intersect to nothing. Measured on the live model: 111 match_rate rows exist, newest at 2026-08-11T04:06:33 with value 99.42, while the table max is 2026-08-11T04:17:09 (producer data_quality_checks, all dq_*).

TWO defects, not one — a naive fix ships the second. The producers write WHOLE percentages (85 means 85%) while the measures' format string is `0.0%`, which expects a fraction. Resolving LatestRun alone would render 99.42 as 9941.8%. Fix both or neither.

Candidate approach (not prescriptive): resolve the latest run per metric via CALCULATE(MAX(refresh_timestamp), ALLEXCEPT(...), metric_name = "..."), or filter on the `producer` column so only silver_to_gold rows compete for the max. Both measures share the identical pattern and must move together — task-061 noticed only Match Rate; Coverage Rate is blank the same way.

Do not commit or push. Per the project rule, a push to main fires a real Fabric publish — the deploy and the in-report confirmation are Erik's half.
acceptanceCriteria: Both [Latest Match Rate] and [Latest Coverage Rate] return a non-blank value, verified against the live published model (offline DEFINE MEASURE evaluation is acceptable evidence for this half, as it was for task-061).

The whole-percentage vs 0.0% format-string mismatch is resolved so the rendered value reads as the true percentage (99.42% for the measured newest match_rate row, not 9941.8% and not 0.99%). State explicitly which side was changed — the measure or the format string.

The latest run is resolved per metric (or per producer) rather than by a table-wide MAX, so a later data_quality_checks append cannot re-blank either measure. Demonstrate this with a case where a dq_* row carries the table max.
Both measures are changed together and remain structurally identical to each other.
docs/dax_measure_library.md:235's 'Both currently return BLANK — known defect' note is replaced with the shipped behaviour; the diagnosis is preserved as history rather than deleted outright.
Erik's half: deploy and confirm in oem_report that both measures render a sensible percentage on a card with no slicer.
notes:
Approved by Erik 2026-08-11 (out-of-spec gate) as one of three confirmed defects that had no task behind them. Diagnosed but deliberately NOT fixed under task-061, which was scoped to Weighted EPI Score; task-061's AC4 recorded it as a defect and stopped there.

The measured evidence in docs/dax_measure_library.md:235 is the starting point — it was produced against the live model, not inferred. Re-measure before changing anything, but do not repeat the diagnosis from scratch.

CAUTION carried from task-061: do not assert DAX semantics without running them. A wrong DIVIDE rationale was supplied in the task-061 dispatch brief, the implementer replaced it with a different wrong one, and only the verifier's measurement caught it.

---

[IMPLEMENTATION 2026-08-12] [Multi-file: 4 files modified] Fixed both [Latest Match Rate] and [Latest Coverage Rate] in gold_quality_history.tmdl, changed together and left structurally identical. Two defects, both addressed: (1) LatestRun is now resolved per metric via CALCULATE(MAX(refresh_timestamp), metric_name = "...") instead of a table-wide MAXX, so a later data_quality_checks append can no longer re-blank them; (2) the whole-percentage/0.0% mismatch is resolved on the MEASURE side via DIVIDE(LatestValue, 100) — the format string 0.0%;-0.0%;0.0% is deliberately UNCHANGED, so these two now match the model's convention of storing a fraction under a percent format (Gap Resolution Rate = 0.4 renders 40.0%, confirmed in gold_gap_registry.tmdl and measured live). EVERY load-bearing claim was measured against the live published model (dataset f57bdfa4-52c9-47a3-b853-dac1d1f76178) via the Power BI executeQueries REST API, not reasoned: the final verification extracted the two measure expressions VERBATIM from the shipped TMDL with a regex and ran that exact text as DEFINE MEASURE — file_match_rate = 0.9941791580255338 rendering "99.4%", file_coverage_rate = 0.9992780825873521 rendering "99.9%", with the still-published old measures returning ISBLANK = TRUE in the same query as the control. AC3's demonstration case is live right now: the table-wide max refresh_timestamp is 2026-08-12T16:06:16.627, owned solely by producer data_quality_checks, carrying ZERO match_rate rows — the exact condition that blanks the old form — and the new measures return values over it anyway. The naive-fix hazard was measured rather than assumed: FORMAT(99.41791580255338, "0.0%;-0.0%;0.0%") = "9941.8%". Filter-context non-regression measured four ways (date slice 99.436% vs 99.418% unfiltered; entity split 99.091%/99.745% averaging to the unfiltered 99.418%; layer=Silver BLANK; producer=data_quality_checks BLANK with producer=silver_to_gold as positive control). producer was evaluated as the discriminator and REJECTED on measurement: 541 of 3,361 rows carry a NULL producer (all at or before 2026-07-22T19:53:09.09), so a producer filter would silently drop the table's history, whereas metric_name is populated on every row (0 blanks, positive control 3,361 total). SELF-REVIEW: verified the TMDL byte-level — expression lines carry 3 tabs and property lines 2, matching the file's existing convention and its sibling measures; formatString / displayFolder / lineageTag are untouched context lines on both measures. docs/dax_measure_library.md § 2.7 now documents the shipped behaviour with the two load-bearing points spelled out, and the old diagnosis is PRESERVED as a labelled 'History' blockquote rather than deleted. § 4's DAX-patterns bullet was rewritten because the change made 'MAXX + CALCULATE to isolate the latest pipeline run' factually stale. A docs sweep (with a positive control) found the same stale MAXX phrasing in two summary lines outside the task's declared files_affected — docs/architecture/semantic_model.md:137 and docs/portfolio/PORTFOLIO_ASSETS_README.md:46 — both corrected. The spec has no reference to either measure (probe exit 1, positive control 'Weighted EPI Score' = 1 hit), so no spec change is implied. NOT committed, NOT pushed — HEAD is unchanged at 49e7c28 and all edits are uncommitted working-tree changes. Erik's half remains: deploy and confirm both measures render a sensible percentage on a card with no slicer in oem_report.

ISSUES DISCOVERED (non-blocking, flagged for follow-up): (1) the `az` CLI is broken on this machine — /opt/homebrew/Cellar/azure-cli/2.72.0's venv interpreter (/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.12) no longer exists, worked around read-only by running azure-cli's site-packages under the uv-managed CPython 3.12 already on disk; homebrew untouched. (2) gold_quality_history's external_coverage_rate metric reads 158.33 (i.e. 158.33%) at every recent run — not a coherent coverage rate, suggests a denominator defect in its producer; out of scope here and has no measure over it today, candidate for a new task.
